messages:
hannah: Heads-up: multiple customer tenants reporting SCIM provisioning 403s starting after last night's OIDC client rotation. New users not created, role assignments failing.

ryan-idp: Samples?

hannah: From proxy logs: upstream /scim/v2/Users -> 403 unauthorized_client. Introspection response: {"error":"unauthorized_client"}. Token header shows client_id=0oa_oldclient.

jess-iam: We rotated the client_id+secret and scheduled the old client to be retired 02:00UTC. Were all deploys coordinated?

infra-bot: deploy: connector-config at 2026-03-20T02:02:30Z set ENV CLIENT_ID=0oa_newclient

hannah: Failures are intermittent and tenant scoped which suggests a partial rollout w/ some pods still using old creds. If those pods mint tokens with the old client, IdP rejects them once old client removed.

ryan-idp: Okta note: client deletion will cause token introspection to return unauthorized depending on org settings. Also some downstream sidecars cache client config. Could be stale cache.

jess-iam: Immediate mitigations: 1) re-enable old client as alias in IdP for 12h, 2) pause automated retirement, 3) start coordinated rollout plan. I can open change request for re-enable.

hannah: Also need to run RBAC reconciliation because some SCIM writes partially applied then failed. Plan: run read-only dry-run over affected tenants, then reconcile diffs back to authoritative source.

infra-bot: ticket INFRA-2345 created: add alert for spikes in unauthorized_client and SCIM failure rate >0.5% across prod.

ryan-idp: Long-term: move connector credentials out of env vars -> central config service with hot-refresh and versioned rollouts. Add canary policy where old client remains valid until 100% of pods confirm new config.

jess-iam: Also check KMS audit around rotation window. If secret fetch failed on some pods they might have minted invalid tokens.

hannah: I'll coordinate customer comms and schedule the reconciliation. Reassigning to jess for IdP alias + KMS audit. Infra to update rollout strategy. Will post follow-up.
